name: What is the best toilet height for accessible bathroom remodeling?

mainEntity.name: Should an accessible remodel use a comfort-height toilet, wall-hung toilet, or standard-height toilet?
mainEntity.text: Should an accessible remodel use a comfort-height toilet, wall-hung toilet, or standard-height toilet?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most accessible bathroom remodels, a comfort-height toilet is the easiest upgrade because the seat height is closer to what many adults find comfortable for sitting and standing. It is often a simple, cost-effective improvement that works well in aging-in-place projects. A wall-hung toilet can be an even more refined solution in a modern remodel because it saves floor space and allows the height to be set more precisely, but it also requires in-wall carrier framing and careful rough-in planning. Standard-height toilets are usually less convenient for users with limited mobility. The final choice should depend on the user’s transfer ability, the available space, and whether the wall can support the needed framing. In tight bathrooms, toilet placement matters as much as toilet style, because side clearance and grab-bar positioning must still work together.
acceptedAnswer.description: A comfort-height toilet is often the most practical choice because it is easier to sit down on and stand up from. A wall-hung toilet can also work well when paired with the right mounting height and clear floor space, but it requires more detailed planning.
